subject: History of USA
title: 15. The Progressive Era: Theodore Roosevelt and Woodrow Wilson

segments.text: Progressives were never one unified ideology — Roosevelt and Wilson used federal power differently, and Progressive reform expanded regulation while simultaneously failing, and in Wilson’s case actively worsening, racial equality — both achievement and exclusion must appear in a strong answer.

blocks.text: Why Progressivism Emerged, and Roosevelt’s Square Deal

segments.text: Large corporations, unsafe food, urban poverty, political machines and labour conflict convinced many middle-class and activist groups that older laissez-faire approaches were insufficient; investigative journalists (“muckrakers”) exposed corruption and corporate abuse, building political pressure for regulation.
argued government should mediate between labour, business and the public, using antitrust law more actively while distinguishing “good” from “bad” trusts; his administration passed the
Pure Food and Drug Act and Meat Inspection Act (1906)
and greatly expanded conservation and federal resource management.

blocks.text: Wilson’s New Freedom and Constitutional Reform

segments.text: initially emphasised restoring competition through reduced tariffs, banking reform, and strengthened antitrust law; the
Federal Reserve Act and Clayton Antitrust Act (both 1913–14)
were major institutional achievements. Progressive-era constitutional amendments established the federal income tax, direct election of senators (
), prohibition, and women’s suffrage — reflecting demands for more responsive government and social regulation.

Many reformers ignored or reinforced racial discrimination, and Wilson’s own administration tolerated segregation in federal workplaces — Progressive reform expanded regulation without delivering equal rights to all Americans, a limitation essential to state explicitly rather than omit.

items.text: Roosevelt’s and Wilson’s respectively distinct approaches to regulating corporate power, both using expanded federal authority but with different emphases.

Do not treat Progressives as one unified party or ideology.
Do not present antitrust policy as the destruction of all big business; regulation and competition were more common goals.
Do not omit race; exclusion is essential to evaluating Progressive reform.
